title: Build the regional switch's layout from its field table

blocks.text: Your client is getting a second link, to a regional debit switch. Its layout differs from the acquirer's in four rows, and `SwitchPackager` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/SwitchPackager.java` already has every other row. Finish the four methods marked `TODO`. Each returns the field packager for one row, and the comment above each method quotes the row from the switch's specification:

rows: n..19, LLVAR. Length and digits in BCD.
ans 8. Text on this switch is EBCDIC.
n 3, BCD, left-justified (the filler nibble last)

blocks.text: The specification comes with sample messages. Here is its sign-on, for code `001`:
When you're done, the switch's samples read as the specification documents them and pack back to the same bytes. About four lines in total.

cases.says: a message with every field of the layout unpacks to the values it was packed with
the switch's sample sign-on reads as code 001 and packs back to the same bytes, because the filler nibble of field 70 is on the side the switch puts it
the switch's sample purchase reads its PAN and amount, because the PAN's BCD length counts digits
the switch's sample echo reads its terminal ID, because the switch's text is EBCDIC
the switch's sample PIN block reads as eight bytes, because a b 64 field travels as raw bytes and not as hex text

origin.section: 13.5 A Round Trip Can't Check the Layout; the Specification's Sample Can

concepts: An odd number of BCD digits carries a filler nibble whose side is the pad setting, and both ends must agree; only odd-length values are affected.
A field packager's class name gives the encoding, the length rule and the type of a specification row; B means BCD, and IFA_BINARY sends bytes as hex text.
A BCD length prefix counts digits for numeric fields and bytes for text and binary fields, and the wrong choice can misread a message without an error.
A round trip can't find a wrong layout because the packager reads back what it wrote; a test from the specification's sample bytes, checking values, bytes used and bytes repacked, can.
